Anthropic IPO — Investment Committee MemoProposed issuer: Anthropic PBC  |  Proposed ticker: ANT  |  Data as of 2026-11-05  |  US$ millions unless noted  |  Internal discussion material1. Summary and Key ConclusionsFY2024 revenue was 386 and FY2025 revenue 4,585 (4,585/386−1 = +1,087.8%, about 11.9x); 9M2026 revenue was 33,242, up 1,206.2% from 2,545 in 9M2025. Quarterly revenue was 4,731 / 11,555 / 16,956, totaling 33,242 for the nine months, a clear weighting toward the latter part of the year.9M2026 operating expenses were 34,502: compute and infrastructure 18,808 (56.6% of revenue), personnel 4,863, sales and partnerships 5,529, and other operating and administrative 5,302; the GAAP operating loss was 1,260, an operating margin of −3.8%. The net loss of 104,039 stems mainly from a 94,324 fair-value loss on convertible notes and similar instruments, a non-cash measurement that is not equivalent to cash consumption.Adjusted operating income was 4,081 = −1,260 + 3,255 + 2,086 (stock-based compensation and non-cash charitable contributions), an adjusted operating margin of 12.3% on a non-GAAP basis. The IPO remains proposed under ticker ANT; offer price and share count are unavailable and are not imputed. FY2024/FY2025 are audited; 9M2026 is unaudited.2. This net amount represents only cash received by the company; it is not used for post-money valuation or dilution, and the greenshoe and overallotment are excluded.• New-share dilution: 50,000 ÷ post-money equity value gives 7.69% / 5.26% / 4.00%. The bull case has the largest denominator and therefore the lowest dilution; the option pool and secondary sales are excluded.• Forward P/S: post-money equity value ÷ 2027 scenario revenue gives 9.29x / 10.56x / 11.36x. The multiple rises across all three scenarios because it absorbs both revenue and valuation assumptions; on its own it cannot support a conclusion that the equity is cheap or expensive.• Gap: net debt data was not obtained. The multiples above are equity-basis forward P/S only; they must not be labeled EV/Sales, and they do not constitute a DCF fair value or a price target.Base-case check: 10,800 = 90,000 × 12%; 10.56x = 950,000/90,000; 5.26% = 50,000/950,000. The three margin levels are linked to a declining compute cost ratio; none is extrapolated from disclosed data, so they are assumptions, not forecasts.6. Financial Due Diligence Checklist (6 items, illustrative)The items and staffing below are illustrative and do not represent Anthropic’s actual internal diligence plan.1. Revenue recognition and quarterly concentration: test the contract basis, invoicing and deferred revenue behind 4,731 / 11,555 / 16,956 and the 33,242 nine-month total, and determine whether the concentration reflects compute delivery timing or contract start dates; evidence: S-1/A pp. 24/150.2. Compute and infrastructure cost: 18,808 equals 56.6% of 9M2026 revenue. Obtain unit compute cost, long-term purchase commitments and capacity reservation terms to validate the cost basis for the 2027 margin expansion.3. Personnel and sales efficiency: personnel 4,863 plus sales and partnerships 5,529 total 10,392 (31.3% of revenue); split revenue per head and customer acquisition cost by function.4. Non-cash items: the gap between the 104,039 net loss and 4,081 adjusted operating income comes mainly from the 94,324 fair-value loss; obtain instrument valuation assumptions, lock-up and conversion terms to confirm its non-cash nature.5. Stock-based compensation and non-cash charitable contributions: the basis for the 3,255 and 2,086 charges, their vesting periods and future dilution.6. Proceeds, dilution and data gaps: replace the teaching assumptions (50,000 gross proceeds, 3% fee rate, 48,500 net proceeds and post-money values of 650,000 / 950,000 / 1,250,000) with actual terms, and confirm offer price, share count and option pool; net debt is missing, so no EV/Sales, DCF or comparable-company fair value range is built yet.7.
